tool.name: seqcluster collapse
tool.description: identical small RNA reads into unique sequences with counts
tool.command: ## seqcluster picks gzip vs plain text from the file extension, and names its ## output after the input basename #if $input.is_of_type('fastqsanger.gz') #set $reads = 'reads.fastq.gz' #else #set $reads = 'reads.fastq' #end if ln -s '$input' '$reads' && mkdir -p collapsed && seqcluster collapse --fastq '$reads' --min $min --out collapsed && mv collapsed/reads_trimmed.fastq '$output'

param.name: input
param.label: Trimmed small RNA reads
param.help: Adapter-trimmed reads. Reads of 15 nt or shorter are dropped.

param.label: Minimum number of copies
param.help: Unique sequences seen fewer times than this are dropped. Values above 1 can bias downstream analysis.

tool.help:
## What it does
`seqcluster collapse` merges identical reads in a small RNA FASTQ file into one record per unique sequence. This is the collapsing step used by nf-core/smrnaseq before mapping reads for seqcluster and mirtop.
Each output record is named `seq_<index>_x<count>`, where `<count>` is the number of input reads with that sequence. The quality string is the per-position average of the merged reads' qualities. The index counts every unique sequence, including ones that were filtered out, so it can have gaps.
## Input
Adapter-trimmed small RNA reads in four-line FASTQ format (plain or gzipped).
- Reads of 15 nt or shorter are always dropped. seqcluster 1.2.9 hard-codes this cutoff, so its `--min_size` option has no effect and is not offered here. - UMI mode is switched on when the first read name contains `UMI_<sequence>` (for example after UMI extraction). Reads are first collapsed per UMI and sequence, then per sequence, so `<count>` becomes the number of distinct UMIs seen with that sequence, not the number of reads. The minimum count applies at both stages. In this mode every read name must carry a UMI tag, or the job fails.
## Output
A FASTQ file with one record per unique sequence that passes the length and minimum-count filters. The file is empty if no sequence passes.
## Example
Input reads:
``` @read1 TGAGGTAGTAGGTTGTATAGTT + FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF @read2 TGAGGTAGTAGGTTGTATAGTT + JJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJ ```
Output:
``` @seq_1_x2 TGAGGTAGTAGGTTGTATAGTT + HHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH ```
